steps.title: Qwen3.8-27B judges a frozen set of 32 image and 32 video cases twice at one commit and gives the same letters, its soft shares within a tolerance declared first
steps.rationale:
A paired comparison counts wins and losses case by case (skill.md:257). A judge that answers differently from run to run turns ties into wins and losses that no change made. Repeated tokens are held for Qwen3.5-9B serving (qwen35_9b_serving_smoke_test.go:151-155) and repeated media bytes for Krea (TestServedPictureKeepsItsSession), but never for the judge through its projector. Some kernels accumulate with atomicAdd (kernels/cuda/ops_f32_elementwise.cuh:691), whose order of addition can vary from run to run.

Serves: held-out-quality; every judged comparison's verdict.
Disappears: a win or loss the judge made up.
Evidence: two runs of the judge on the frozen cases give the same letters and soft shares within the declared tolerance.

steps.title: A generated-media judgement keeps each answer under the judge's identity, the media's digest and the question, and a later run on the same inputs replays it instead of asking
steps.rationale:
evaluateGeneratedAnswer asks every case on every run (internal/evaluation/generated_answer.go:176-186). The multiple-choice, instruction-rule and sampled-answer suites already reuse answers keyed by everything an answer depends on (internal/evaluation/observation.go:60-104, held by TestAnswersOutliveOnlyTheCommitsThatLeaveTheirCodeUnchanged). A judged question costs about 27 s for TIFA images (3b20a6e87) and about 6.3 s for video (the Wan student's run on 2026-11-08), so the 415-question TIFA suite takes about three hours of the card. A reference model's outputs do not change between comparisons. video-judge/same-settings judges Wan's base, and every later preset, eight-bit or step-cache candidate is compared with the same reference, so the reference's answers need asking only once.

items.title: Image embeddings screen a media change in minutes: each case's output is compared with the reference path's, and each clip's frames with their neighbours

budget.reason: Estimated after a survey of the code, at about twice what a first sketch of the steps counts, since this week's rows landed at two to six times the counts they were filed with (wan-few-step 300 -> 1100, sampling-split 400 -> 1700, umt5-resident 336 -> 1750): a screen command over vitencoder's card path with a floor read from a second seed, and a frame-to-frame measure carried to the video cells.

steps.title: cmd/evaluate -screen embeds a candidate path's outputs and the reference path's at the same prompts and seeds with webssl-dino300m on the card, and fails the cases where the candidate lies farther from the reference than a second seed of the same prompt does
steps.rationale:
internal/vitencoder embeds on the card (vitencoder.Card, internal/vitencoder/card.go:17-33; 1024 dimensions for webssl-dino300m). Its only metric today is retrieval over real frames (internal/evaluation/image_retrieval.go:120-164). No embedding compares two generated images, and FD-DINOv2 (rae-small-models/fd-dinov2) compares distributions, not cases. The fast-path rows (eight-bit-attention, w8a8-gemm, step-cache, light-vae, video-decode-overlap) change values beyond any golden's tolerance, so each is admitted by a judged paired comparison (skill.md:257). That costs the renders plus 6 to 27 s a question.

The floor needs no chosen constant. Two seeds of one prompt are two valid outputs, so a candidate output farther from its reference than another seed has lost what the prompt asked. The screen counts those cases with tensorstats.ExactPairedBinary, and only a candidate it passes goes to the judged comparison. The fast-path rows can name it in their checks.

Serves: setup-steps; card hours per fast-path change.
Disappears: a broken fast path found only after hours of rendering and judging.
Evidence: on a fixture, a candidate with a corrupted step fails the screen and one that rounds differently passes.
Batch: device lane.

steps.title: Every generated or edited clip records the similarity of each frame's embedding to the next, its mean and lowest, beside its judged score, its floor read from the same measure over the source clips the suite's captions describe
steps.rationale:
The video judge asks two questions a clip about its content (internal/evaluation/generated_video_matching.go:127-195). Nothing measures how a clip moves, and no Go file measures flicker or change from frame to frame. LiveEdit and the Wan student generate in chunks of three latent frames. long-video's rolling window and video-decode-overlap's chunked decode join chunks. A seam or flicker shows as a clip's lowest neighbour similarity, which no caption question sees. The VidGen source clips hold real motion for each caption, so the floor is read from data, not chosen.

Serves: held-out-quality for every video generator and editor.
Disappears: a seam between chunks that no measure sees.
Evidence: a fixture clip with one frame repeated and one replaced shows both in its lowest similarity, and the video cells carry the measure.
Batch: device lane.

items.title: Unlimited-OCR reads the text each image generator draws, and the drawn-text suite scores the characters it read back, over briefs written by seeded code

budget.reason: Estimated after a survey of the code, at about twice what a first sketch of the steps counts, since this week's rows landed at two to six times the counts they were filed with (wan-few-step 300 -> 1100, sampling-split 400 -> 1700, umt5-resident 336 -> 1750): the OCR model's projector path opened for the suite, a character score carried to the scorecard, and a brief writer over word and number lists.

steps.title: cmd/evaluate reads an image's text with Unlimited-OCR through projector.DeepSeekOCRRunner, recording its model and projector identities with what it read
steps.rationale:
Unlimited-OCR's vision path exists (internal/projector/deepseekocr.go:41, registered at internal/projector/prompt.go:295). Only TestUnlimitedOCRProductionParity holds it (internal/adaptiveparity/unlimited_ocr_windows_test.go:55-175: an exact 200-token prefix, row coordinates within 1 and an edit distance of at most 1 per row), and that test opens the projector directly. The served row is text -> text (README.md:137). docs/verification/text-vision-coverage.json:66 says document recognition is not claimed, and compatibility.json holds it pending-fixture. Qwen3.8-27B can read text through its projector, but it is the suite's judge. A separate reader keeps the reading and the judging two instruments, and a dedicated OCR model reads more cheaply than a 27B judge's 27 s a question.

Serves: held-out-quality for every image generator.
Disappears: an OCR vision path no command runs.
Evidence: the reader reads the parity test's page within that test's bounds, and a drawn-text picture's reading records the reader's identities.
Batch: device lane.

steps.title: The drawn-text suite scores each picture by the share of its brief's characters the reader read back, title, three lines and small print, beside the judge's choice and soft share, and the scorecard reads it
steps.rationale:
The suite asks the judge which of four near texts a picture holds (internal/evaluation/drawn_text.go:20, with near titles at :116 and near numbers at :151). SenseNova scores 100 of 100, the whole suite (README.md:143), so no change to SenseNova can show a gain there, and a picture with one wrong letter in its small print scores the same as one with none. The score is one minus the edit distance over the length of the brief's text, per picture. It is computed by code once the reader has read. Krea and MOSS draw text too, so the score applies to every image generator.

Serves: held-out-quality for every image generator.
Disappears: a text-drawing suite at its ceiling.
Evidence: a fixture picture with one character wrong scores below one with none, and the scorecard's drawn-text cell carries the character score.
Batch: host lane.

steps.title: Seeded code writes drawn-text briefs from word and number lists, so a suite holds as many pictures as it asks for, the 20 held briefs first
steps.rationale:
PickDrawnText refuses more briefs than drawn_briefs.json holds, which is 20 (internal/evaluation/drawn_text.go:191-193). Twenty pictures give a paired sign test (tensorstats.ExactPairedBinary) at most 20 cases that can differ. A brief is a title with two swappable words, three number lines and a line of small print (internal/evaluation/drawn_briefs.json). Seeded code can fill that shape from lists, as internal/evaluation/composed_cases.go fills TIFA's composed cases from composed_atoms.json. The 20 held briefs stay the first 20, so earlier readings remain comparable.

steps.title: The driver lands a worker's step once its check passes, as it lands a run step, and the worker's prompt no longer asks it to run a command its six tools cannot
steps.rationale:
The default prompt tells the worker to commit through go run ./cmd/loop -land (cmd/loop/init_config.go:53-55). But the worker starts with --tools "" and only the six tools of cmd/loop -tools (read_file, edit_file, run_check, run_tests, show_step, run_probe; cmd/loop/tools.go:55-115), none of which lands. The driver lands only a run step itself (RunCommand, cmd/loop/main.go:444-462) and otherwise waits for the worker to land (internal/loop/driver.go:50-51, 293-299). So a worker with no shell cannot finish a code step. On this machine .overgo-runtime/loop.json still grants the worker Bash and Edit, which is how a step lands today.

Serves: setup-steps; model calls per landing.

steps.title: cmd/loop's local worker sends the step's prompt and the six tools to overgo's own chat route and runs each tool call the model makes, and Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q6_K passes a fixture step with it
steps.rationale:
overgo serves /v1/chat/completions and /v1/messages with tools (internal/server/routes.go:48-57, internal/server/anthropic_tools.go), constraining a call to the tool grammar for GGUF templates that use <function=...> or <tool_call> (internal/inference/chat_tool_grammar.go:39-49), as the Qwen GGUFs do. The six tools already live in cmd/loop/tools.go, and the driver's config gives each worker its own command and environment (cmd/loop/main.go:81-97). Nothing connects a worker to overgo's server today. A worker of overgo's own needs only the step's prompt and the six tools, not a client prompt written for Claude and resent every turn.

Serves: model calls per landing; the loop runs on overgo's own inference.
Disappears: a driver whose every worker is an outside service.

steps.title: Steps that landed since 2026-11-01 with one Go test as their check are replayed, each from its parent commit in a worktree of its own, recording each worker's passes, attempts, tool calls and wall per step
steps.rationale:
No harness runs a local model as an agent on tasks and scores it. BindAgentTrajectoryPlan (internal/evaluation/plan.go:198-213, called from cmd/loop/evidence.go:136-180) binds trajectories and names ten scorers that nothing computes. The nearest scored suite is single function calls (internal/evaluation/function_call.go, where needle scores 0.255 on 400). A landed step is a task with a known answer: its parent commit, its plan step and its check, which must fail at the parent (skill.md:121) and passed at the landing. Replaying them measures each worker on overgo's own work, on the same steps: Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q6_K, Qwen3.5-9B-Q8_0 and the Claude worker.

Serves: model calls per landing.
Disappears: a worker ranked with no measurement.

steps.title: loop.json's default workers list puts the local model first for the kinds of step where its replayed pass rate makes its attempts, plus the Claude worker's on its failures, take less wall than the Claude worker alone, and the Claude worker after it
steps.rationale:
The driver already ranks workers cheapest first and moves a step it cannot pass, with its failures, to the next (internal/loop/driver.go:32-34 and 220-224; skill.md:50). It was written because overgo is to run on a much weaker model. What is missing is the measurement of where a weaker model pays. A step's kind is the top directory of its listed files and whether it needs the card. The ordering follows from the replay's pass rates and walls, with no threshold chosen by hand.

Serves: model calls per landing.
Disappears: a strong worker spent on steps a local model passes.
Evidence: given replay records, the default config orders the workers per kind by expected wall, and a kind with no local passes keeps the Claude worker first.

items.title: CFG-Zero*, the guidance interval, APG and NAG are guider functions written from their papers, each a preset admitted per model by its held-out suite

budget.reason: Re-estimated 2026-11-08 in one pass, at about three times the first estimate: the campaign's steps came in at 3 to 7 times theirs (served 1878 of 447, interface 1010 of 400, causal-t2v 653 of 300), a rewritten loop counting whole, and a step that measures carries its cell through the timing chain (internal/media, capabilityruntime, servingattempt, runrecord, cmd/recipe, scorecard).

steps.title: CFG-Zero* and a guidance interval run on Wan's 50-step path, MOSS and SenseNova, with a shift sweep on Wan, each read against its suite
steps.rationale:
CFG-Zero* (arXiv 2503.18886, Apache-2.0) rescales the unconditioned prediction by its optimal projection and zeroes the first steps; it raised Wan 1.3B's VBench total from 80.52 to 80.91 at no cost. A guidance interval (arXiv 2404.07724) applies guidance only in the middle of the noise range and drops the unconditioned pass elsewhere, about 15 to 20 of MOSS's 100 passes. Wan's shift is 5 here (the reference script) and 8 to 12 on the model card, so a sweep of 3 to 12 is a cheap quality reading. MOSS's negative branch skips layer 22, so every change is re-read on its suite.

Each lands as a named preset; the reference presets are unchanged.

Serves: held-out-quality, first-output.
Disappears: nothing.
Evidence: each preset's per-case sign test against its model's reference on its suite is recorded, and only a preset that does not lower quality is offered.
Batch: device lane.

steps.title: APG replaces the guidance combine for MOSS and SenseNova as a preset
steps.rationale:
MOSS and SenseNova guide at 3 to 4. APG (Sadat et al., 2024) splits the guidance delta into parallel and orthogonal parts, clamps its norm and adds momentum, cutting oversaturation at no extra pass; on DiT-XL/2 it took FID from 19.14 to 9.34 at guidance 4. It is written from the paper, never from ComfyUI's node.

Serves: held-out-quality.
Disappears: nothing.
Evidence: the preset's sign test against each model's reference is recorded.
Batch: device lane.

steps.title: NAG restores negative prompts at guidance 1 on Krea-2-Turbo and the Wan student
steps.rationale:
Krea-2-Turbo runs without guidance and the Wan student at guidance 1, so neither honours a negative prompt; raising guidance on Turbo over-cooks it. NAG (arXiv 2505.21179; MIT code) extrapolates in attention space with L1 normalisation: ImageReward rose from 1.029 to 1.099 on Flux-Schnell and from 0.944 to 1.118 on SD3.5-Large-Turbo, at 43 to 87% more time. Krea's published settings are phi 4.0, tau 2.5, alpha 0.25.

Serves: held-out-quality; a capability the distilled models lack.
Disappears: nothing.
Evidence: a negative prompt changes the attention context only through NAG, and the preset's sign test is recorded.

steps.title: The recorder turns MOSS_IMAGE_ULTRA_WORKFLOW.json into ComfyUI's API request: its 24 subgraphs flattened, Set/Get links resolved, bypassed nodes dropped, widget values named from /object_info
steps.rationale:
The owner decided on 2026-11-05 that the golden for MOSS Ultra is ComfyUI running C:/Users/jeffm/Downloads/Moss/MOSS_IMAGE_ULTRA_WORKFLOW.json on the files in its own install. The workflow is a saved UI graph, not an API request.

A Go command copies the workflow into fixtures with its hash and builds the API request: subgraphs flattened, KJNodes' Set/Get links resolved, bypassed nodes dropped, each node's widgets_values mapped to input names from ComfyUI's /object_info, one section switched on at a time. It adds only recording nodes: SaveLatent after each sampler, PreviewAny on a BasicScheduler carrying the section's schedule so sigmas are recorded as numbers, and the workflow's own prompt-used outputs. ComfyUI is GPL-3.0; it runs as a separate process and overgo reads only its HTTP answers (the GPL FAQ treats pipes and sockets as communication between separate programs); no ComfyUI source is read or ported.

Disappears: hand-built ComfyUI references.

steps.title: bong_tangent, beta57 and a request's own sigma list are named schedules, bong_tangent's sigmas equal to the recorded ones at 8 and 50 steps and at denoise 0.72
